requirements.title: Formatted connections have the listed changeable modes
requirements.definition: A connection for formatted input/output has the listed changeable modes: blank interpretation, delimiter, sign, leading zero, decimal edit, input/output rounding, pad, and scale factor.

pending.formatted-connection-listed-changeable-m: Use future focused fixtures for each mode after its owning rule is registered; establish a connection and change exactly one mode while using nondefault sentinels to prove the data-transfer effect.

requirements.title: Unformatted connections have no changeable modes
requirements.definition: A connection for unformatted input/output has no changeable modes.

pending.unformatted-connection-no-changeable-mod: Open an unformatted external connection and first establish it with INQUIRE(OPENED=) into a logical initialized to .false. and INQUIRE(FORM=) into a default-character variable prefilled with a distinct nonblank sentinel, expecting OPENED=.true. and FORM='UNFORMATTED'. Then INQUIRE on the same unit with BLANK=, DECIMAL=, DELIM=, LEADING_ZERO=, PAD=, ROUND=, and SIGN= variables each prefilled with a distinct sentinel not equal to 'UNDEFINED'; 12.10.2.6, 12.10.2.7, 12.10.2.8, 12.10.2.15, 12.10.2.21, 12.10.2.28, and 12.10.2.30 respectively require the assigned value 'UNDEFINED' when the connection is not for formatted input/output. Those 12.10.2.x rules provide the observation mechanism; the owned facet remains the 12.5.2 p1 rule that an unformatted connection has no changeable modes.

requirements.title: Connection mode values are established when the connection is initiated
requirements.definition: Mode values are established when the connection is initiated: by explicit or implicit OPEN specifiers for an OPEN-initiated connection, or by the values implied by an initial OPEN without corresponding keywords for internal or preconnected files.

pending.open-established-mode-values: Open a scratch external formatted file with one explicit mode specifier and one omitted specifier, then perform a transfer that distinguishes the explicit mode from the default after initializing all data/buffers to sentinels.
pending.internal-preconnected-initial-mode-value: For an internal file or INPUT_UNIT/OUTPUT_UNIT, observe only a mode whose default is fixed by its owning OPEN/specifier rule; do not assume processor-dependent defaults.

requirements.definition: The scale factor cannot be explicitly specified in an OPEN statement and is implicitly zero.

requirements.title: A subsequent OPEN can change external-file connection modes
requirements.definition: The modes of a connection to an external file can be changed by a subsequent OPEN statement that modifies the connection.

requirements.title: Data transfer specifiers and edit descriptors can temporarily change modes and reset afterward
requirements.definition: A connection mode can be temporarily changed by a corresponding data transfer keyword or edit descriptor. Keyword specifiers take effect at statement execution, edit descriptors when encountered in format processing, and modes reset to their prior values when the data transfer statement terminates.

pending.data-transfer-keyword-temporary-mode: Use a data-transfer keyword for a mode with a known contrasting effect; initialize targets to nondefault sentinels and compare only the transfer governed by that statement.
pending.edit-descriptor-temporary-mode: Use an edit descriptor that changes a mode partway through a format, with adjacent fields chosen to differ; output buffers start with impossible # sentinels.
pending.mode-reset-after-data-transfer: Perform a second transfer after the temporary one without the keyword/descriptor and with fresh sentinels; expect the pre-transfer mode effect, proving reset rather than persistent mutation.

States that unformatted connections have no changeable modes.
Mode establishment differs for OPEN-initiated and other connections.
OPEN establishes mode values explicitly or implicitly.
Internal and preconnected files use initial OPEN implied values.
Defines the scale-factor initial value and absence from OPEN specification.
Permission for subsequent OPEN mode changes.
Temporary keyword/edit-descriptor changes and reset are split.
